quest.title: Shifting Earth and Lost Threads Come to Light
quest.description: The evidence at the mining site suggests that the miners followed the road north. You follow the trail, gradually closing in on them.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Head to Lingju Pass to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, there are tracks here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These must have been left by the miners!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Let us make our way to the end of Lingju Pass. If there are no footprints there, it would suggest that the miners are still within the pass itself. However, if we find new tracks, we can follow them wherever they may lead.

talks.objective: Look for more clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Footprints!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It would appear that they made their way through Lingju Pass and kept moving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we follow their footprints, we should be able to find where they went!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, seen any miners?

dialogues.speaker: Ling
dialogues.text: ...It must have been about four or five days ago. There were a few men who came through here carrying baskets and picks... I guess that could have been them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! That's them!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Four or five days ago? It appears that they were moving slower than we'd anticipated. Traversing the geography of Lingju Pass must have held them up.

dialogues.speaker: Ling
dialogues.text: It was so strange! Four big guys with lifeless expressions... It was like they were in some sort of trance! And there was a child staggering in front of them...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Huh, this child... Did you see what they look like?

dialogues.speaker: Ling
dialogues.text: I caught a glimpse... blue hair, short. I think... I think it was a girl! She wasn't smiling, in fact she looked very serious.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: And they took this road?

dialogues.speaker: Ling
dialogues.text: Yes, they followed it straight from here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go after them!

talks.objective: Follow the road and keep up the pursuit

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: Those monsters were so aggressive — they must have noticed me walking through! Before I knew it they were all over me... Thank you all for saving me.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: My name is Wanyu, I belong to Liyue's Shenglu Hall. I head up our human culture and civilization research.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You sure you're not... a miner?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: A miner?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. We're looking for a group of four strong fellas carrying mining equipment.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: I... I think I saw those people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really!?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: Yes. I set off from Nantianmen the day before yesterday heading for Lingju Pass. About halfway there I came across some people — a few men and a child.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you be a bit more specific?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: I was in a hurry, I didn't get a good look. I'm afraid I'm not even sure what they looked like... apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I think that's all we needed to hear. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: I hope it's useful to you!

dialogues.speaker: Wanyu
dialogues.text: I'd better get going, there's a conference I need to attend. Again, thank you all for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to this scholar, the miners were heading for Nantianmen.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Can we be absolutely sure that it was the men that we're looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A child with a group of adults! Sounds pretty close to Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It could easily have been a different group.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... but...

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Hey, perhaps that rock over there can tell us more!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha! Paimon nearly forgot about our secret weapon!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: It looks promising, I'll do my best.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: It's the same group alright. They followed this road.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Haha, Mr. Kun Jun, your stone-seeing is something I won't forget in a hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: I suppose it is an asset, though I rarely find a use for it. But praise from Mr. Zhongli is high praise indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a good thing we brought our "Kun Jun compass" along! We would've lost all sense of direction a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Hahaha, you think so? I guess it's been a worthwhile trip then.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: It feels like... like we're cracking a criminal case. It's a lot of fun.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Be that as it may, we would do well to keep our guards high.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Four fully-grown men in a trance-like state... walking ceaselessly day and night... over hills and mountains... led by a child... This is no ordinary incident.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Oh! You're quite right, Mr. Zhongli. We should have our wits about us.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: That's not all. Our scholar was attacked by Geovishap Hatchlings, but the level of aggression they exhibited was... unusual.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: We have encountered many clues along the way. So far they've pointed us in the right direction.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hmm, the miners headed in the direction of Nantianmen the day before yesterday. From here they would have had to navigate a perilous mountain road. If their destination is indeed Nantianmen, we should be able to catch up with them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! No time to lose!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I left a mark in the vicinity just now. If Uncle Dai does pass through here, it should guide him to us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Clever thinking! A classic Zhongli move.

talks.objective: Head to Nantianmen and look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: There's a basket lying here too... This must be one of the miners.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Hello? Can you hear us?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Judging by his appearance, he must have collapsed from exhaustion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we wake him up?

dialogues.speaker: Miner
dialogues.text: I can... I can still dig...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp* Sounds like he's whispering something...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It seems that he thinks he still has work to do. Something's not right.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: There's a camp nearby. We should take him there and monitor his condition before deciding our next move.

choices.text: He looks like he's trying to stand up.

talks.objective: Take the miner to a nearby camp to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is he? H—He won't die, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: He's worked himself into a stupor. Thankfully, he's not in serious danger.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did he get so exhausted?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon heard him talking about digging for something. Did he dig himself into this state?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It's certainly a possibility.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Hm? It looks like there's something in his pocket...

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Are these... ore fragments?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I just witnessed the memories within these ore fragments. This person brought these fragments out of the mine. He's one of the four that we're searching for.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: How he came to be here is what we need to understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So he was kidnapped, and then... abandoned here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if they didn't need him, why bring him all the way out here?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Unless something happened... something that led him to fall behind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's had enough! This is too mysterious!

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Oh! Wait a moment! Seeing these fragments has jogged my memory — I have something for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it? Ooh! Is it a present?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Something... for us?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: As I mentioned, before I met Uncle Dai I was in a daze. After setting out with you on this case, it feels like a fog is lifting.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I was so happy when Uncle Dai enlisted you to help. I would never have managed to track down these clues by myself.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: These are some crystals that I bought from the market. Not any old crystals mind you — this purity is extraordinarily rare! One for each of you. A memory, if you will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's beautiful... Oh — and the colors change as you turn it! It's like a different crystal from each angle.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: But of course, take it.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: And this one is for Mr. Zhongli.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Huh? I—Is something wrong? Not to your liking?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: On the contrary... I just hadn't anticipated receiving a gift during the current circumstances.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But, thank you. I will take good care of it.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I'm pleased you like them. It's nice to be able to give a gift that others can appreciate.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Oh! I see more rocks over there. You should all get some rest, I'm going to walk awhile — perhaps there are more memories to uncover.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure like rocks, huh Kun Jun...

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Ores are the crystals of the earth, the sediment of time itself. I feel at peace among them.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Get some rest, and call me when you're ready to set off. I won't be far.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He'll be okay on his own, right?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Rest easy, I surveyed the area. There's no danger here.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Oh, however, there is something I wanted to discuss with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's with the seriousness all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Traveler... Does Dragonfall mean anything to you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean the ore that Kun Jun's looking for? What's so special about it?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Dragonfall is an incredibly rare ore used in forging. The majority of regular crystals are formed in high-temperature environments. Dragonfall, on the other hand, is formed as a product of elemental reactions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Elemental reactions can produce material objects?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed they can. However, only a minority can survive for long periods of time.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Dragonfall first emerged in the midst of a great battle, thousands of years ago. Powerful clashes of elemental energy gave birth to elemental crystals. When the fighting ceased, these geological remnants were miraculously preserved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cooool...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: And yet they are crystal creations all the same, few and far between, relatively unknown. A few hundred years ago, they were virtually mined into obscurity.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Why is it then, that a citizen of Liyue now wishes to strike upon ore that has long since vanished from the earth?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! If he knows of its existence, surely he knows all of it's already been mined?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Weird... Paimon doesn't get it...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: There are those in the mining trade who retain a keen interest in Dragonfall. But for someone like Mr. Kun Jun... whose motivations for seeking it are unclear even unto himself... it's practically unheard-of.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps he has ulterior motives.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ulterior motives... *gasp* Is he a villain!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: A conclusion that is presently impossible to reach. We must watch... and wait.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Don't forget, rescuing those miners is the primary objective. As for anything else... Sooner or later the tide will reveal the lie of the land.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: We're drawing closer to our goal. I believe we should continue to follow this road through. Now that we've found one, the others won't be far away.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: When you're well-rested, call Mr. Kun Jun over to us. We still have more investigation ahead.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: We should ensure this miner is settled here at the camp. Once we've brought this matter to a close, we can return and attend to him. I suggest we leave a note for Uncle Dai. If he does find the camp he'll know what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stone
dialogues.text: (It looks like... some sort of Cor Lapis?)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stone
dialogues.text: (It was able to record the information we needed. A curious stone, indeed.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stone
dialogues.text: (This rock is no different from ordinary Cor Lapis... and yet, Kun Jun was able to see a memory through it.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stone
dialogues.text: (It was thanks to this sort of rock that we were able to find some clues.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, have you seen anyone dressed like a miner around here?

dialogues.speaker: Yonggui
dialogues.text: A miner? I'm afraid not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Let's try someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! Have you seen any miners nearby? About this tall — four of them?

dialogues.speaker: Wei
dialogues.text: Stop bothering me! Can't you see I'm cloud-watching?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez! A little grumpy, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever, let's go ask someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Yonggui
dialogues.text: *sigh* My legs don't work like they used to... Guess my age is catching up with me...

dialogues.speaker: Wei
dialogues.text: You again... I'm busy!

dialogues.speaker: Ling
dialogues.text: I've never seen anything like it... Were they sleepwalking? So bizarre...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Over here on the ground! Is this one of the missing people?
